input_signals.name: Equity-Financed Intangible Expansion
input_signals.hypothesis: Balance-sheet intangibles that expand precisely when the firm is issuing equity indicate stock-financed acquisition of soft assets at inflated valuations rather than organically created intangible capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Managers issue overvalued equity and deploy it into acquired intangibles and goodwill, so the joint occurrence of issuance and intangible growth is a sharper overvaluation marker than either component alone. The multiplicative rank form fires only when both conditions hold, capturing the conditional market-timing mechanism instead of the additive average of two weak effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), rank( growth( intan, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Acquired Intangibles
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, intan), 1), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net long-term debt raised to buy goodwill and acquired intangibles creates leveraged claims backed by non-collateralizable soft assets, which subsequently underperform through impairment risk and debt overhang on future innovation.
input_signals.reasoning: Goodwill additions financed with new long-term debt combine two fragilities: an unverifiable asset and a hard fixed claim, so integration failure triggers write-offs while the debt service crowds out productive spending. Using goodwill where reported and total intangibles otherwise keeps the acquired-intangible interpretation without a blanket coverage patch.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), rank( ratio( delta( coalesce( gdwl, intan ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance Timed Away From Innovation
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issued in a year when the firm's own R&D intensity is at a five-year low is not financing innovation; it is opportunistic capital raised while the intangible investment program is idle, which is the clearest expression of overvaluation-driven issuance.
input_signals.reasoning: TS_RANK normalizes R&D against the firm's own history, so the signal is not a cross-sectional R&D-intensity anomaly in disguise; it measures within-firm timing mismatch between the financing event and the innovation cycle. The multiplicative form activates only when large issuance coincides with an innovation lull, distinguishing genuine R&D funding rounds (which should be neutral or good) from paper-selling.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( xrd, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Financing Surplus Over Intangible Needs
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(ADD(xrd, DELTA(intan, 1)), at)), 5)), INDICATOR(RATIO(ADD(xrd, intan), at), 0.05))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among intangible-intensive firms, external capital raised well in excess of contemporaneous intangible investment (R&D expense plus the increase in the intangible balance) represents financing without a matching innovation use, i.e., valuation-driven issuance; conversely, intangible spending exceeding external funds raised is self-financed innovation.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are scaled by total assets rather than by a near-zero intangible base, so the measure is a bounded financing-need gap rather than an inverse-intangible-intensity artifact, and 5% symmetric winsorization removes the residual tail influence the critic flagged. The indicator restricts active values to firms with a meaningful intangible base (above 5% of assets), placing non-intangible firms at a neutral zero so that both portfolio legs are drawn from the population where the mechanism actually applies.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( add( xrd, delta( intan, 1 ) ), at ) ), 5 ) ), indicator( ratio( add( xrd, intan ), at ), 0.05 ) )

input_signals.name: Paper-For-Intangibles Versus Cash-For-Shares
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(SUB(MIN(RATIO(sstk, at), MUL(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at), INDICATOR(DELTA(intan, 1), 0))), MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), MUL(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at)), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(intan, 1)), 0)))), 2)
input_signals.hypothesis: The overvaluation signature is equity issued and intangible assets simultaneously built up (paper exchanged for soft assets), while the mirror case — cash returned to shareholders as the intangible base is written down or divested — reflects disciplined redeployment; the return spread should run from the first group to the second.
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator gates make each MIN a conjunction of two strictly non-negative, identically asset-scaled dollar flows, so the previous defect — a bottom leg populated by intangible impairments rather than by the absence of stock-financed expansion — is eliminated. Subtracting the symmetric repurchase-with-intangible-contraction term gives the signal a populated, economically meaningful negative tail instead of a large tie block at zero, which should improve the reliability of the long-short alpha rather than only the cross-sectional slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( min( ratio( sstk, at ), mul( ratio( delta( intan, 1 ), at ), indicator( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ) ) ), min( ratio( prstkc, at ), mul( neg( ratio( delta( intan, 1 ), at ) ), indicator( neg( delta( intan, 1 ) ), 0 ) ) ) ), 2 )

input_signals.name: Issuance Into the Unrecorded-Intangible Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), RANK(RATIO(intan, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Valuation opacity is greatest where economic intangible capital is large but almost none of it appears on the balance sheet; net equity raised by firms sitting in that expensed-knowledge gap is the hardest for investors to monitor and is where proceeds are most likely to reflect timing rather than verified projects.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg is now a split-immune dollar flow, net share issuance scaled by assets, rather than csho growth, so stock splits and stock dividends can no longer dominate the extreme decile. The conditioning weight is not intangible intensity itself but the *gap* between three-year accumulated R&D and recorded intangibles, so the signal is switched off for transparent firms and for firms whose intangibles are already capitalized, making the effect an identified opacity interaction rather than a monotone restatement of the issuance anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( sub( rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( intan, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity
input_signals.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing should occur when each research dollar is converting into more revenue; net equity raised while revenue per unit of smoothed R&D is on a downward trend is capital raised into a deteriorating innovation franchise and should predict poor returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs gen-0's Productivity-Signed Intangible Financing, whose SIGN switch threw away trend magnitude and whose two-sided structure produced a near-zero alpha (-0.5%, t -0.65); here the productivity trend enters as a bounded, magnitude-preserving rank weight that switches the signal off for firms with improving research productivity. It tests whether the issuance penalty is driven by observable innovation-output decay rather than by the level or timing of research spending.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( sale, ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Goodwill-Built Firms
input_signals.hypothesis: The penalty to equity issuance should be concentrated in firms whose intangible base was purchased rather than created: goodwill-heavy balance sheets combine a history of paying premia with an asset that cannot be verified or liquidated, so new equity raised there is the least monitorable.
input_signals.reasoning: Paired against Signal 1, this asks whether the issuance-intangible interaction lives in *acquired* or *organic* intangible capital — a first-order economic question the archive has not separated, since gen-0's debt-plus-goodwill test mixed instruments and used the failed rank-product form. Treating unreported goodwill as zero is the economically correct convention (no reported goodwill means no acquired intangibles) and lifts coverage well above the R&D-reporter-only signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Financing Accelerating as Intangible Investment Decelerates
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), 2), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(xrd, DELTA(intan, 1)), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The clean market-timing case is divergence in changes: a firm that steps up its external capital raising in the same year that it steps *down* its intangible investment is raising money that demonstrably is not going into innovation, whereas a joint step-up in both is genuine project funding.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 signal compared financing and intangible spending in levels, which mostly ranks firms by their standing business model; this compares their year-over-year *changes*, so the same firm is its own benchmark and the signal fires on a genuine divergence event rather than on a static financing-to-intangible ratio. The deceleration term enters as a bounded rank weight so that firms increasing intangible investment are gated toward zero, preserving the conditional cross-theme element the critic noted was lost when the indicator gate was dropped.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 2 ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( xrd, delta( intan, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance While Losing the Innovation Race
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters for the value of intangible financing is the firm's research position relative to its competitors, not its absolute spending: a firm raising equity while its R&D intensity slips down the industry ranking is funding a losing position in an innovation race, and the market is slow to recognize competitive displacement.
input_signals.reasoning: Every intangible conditioner in the archive is firm-specific (own level, own trend, own history), so competitive position is a genuinely new economic channel and its weight — the one-year change in a firm's within-industry R&D-intensity rank — is continuous, bounded, and free of the tied masses that broke earlier sorts. It should also be cleaner than raw productivity trends because industry ranking automatically nets out sector-wide research cycles and technology-cost shocks that contaminate sale-per-R&D.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( delta( ind_rank( ratio( xrd, sale ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: External Funding Intensity of the Research Program
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is how many dollars of outside capital the firm takes in per dollar it spends on research: a research program financed largely from outside funds is exposed to funding withdrawal and is the natural home of story-driven issuance, whereas a program covered by internal resources is self-validating.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the product architecture entirely and normalizes the financing flow by the intangible flow itself, so the interaction is in the units of the measure rather than in a multiplicative weight — it is not the instrument ablation the critic objected to. The denominator is a three-year average of R&D restricted to reporters (never near zero), the ratio is winsorized at 5% tails, and industry ranking makes the final score bounded and comparable across sectors with very different normal funding-to-research ratios, which addresses the blow-up defect of the gen-0 attempt at a ratio form.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance as Pricing Power Erodes
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross margin is the realized output of brand, customer and organizational capital; equity raised in a year when that margin is compressing is capital raised as the intangible franchise is being competed away, which is the observable, high-coverage counterpart of raising money into a decaying research franchise.
input_signals.reasoning: Every strong archive result is confined to R&D reporters and coverage has never exceeded 6% in that family, whereas sale, cogs, sstk and prstkc are near-universally reported, so this tests whether the same economic interaction survives on a much broader universe with a different intangible proxy — a genuine external-validity test rather than a re-parameterization. Margin change is continuous with no tied mass, avoiding the degenerate-weight failure that broke the goodwill and intangible-contraction sorts.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: New Claims Per Dollar of Total Intangible Capital
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), intan)), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: What existing shareholders should fear is new outside claims issued against a given stock of intangible capital; measuring financing against the *total* intangible base — accumulated research spending plus capitalized intangibles — rather than against the current research flow captures dilution of the knowledge and brand capital that current owners already hold.
input_signals.reasoning: This converts the winning flow-to-flow ratio into a flow-to-stock measure and, critically, admits non-R&D-reporting firms with recorded intangibles by treating unreported research as zero spending, which should roughly double the 5% coverage of the best archive signals and test whether the mechanism is specific to research-driven firms or general to intangible-heavy ones. The denominator is a non-negative capital stock rather than a differenced flow, so it cannot change sign or collapse toward zero the way earlier intangible-investment denominators did.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), intan ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Outside-Funded Research While Sliding Down the Industry
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5), RANK(NEG(SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)), LAG(IND_RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)), 2)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose research is paid for out of outside money while its research intensity slides down the industry ranking over a two-year span is funding a losing competitive position; the funding leg should be measured per research dollar, because the same absolute raise means something very different for a firm spending heavily on research than for one that barely researches at all.
input_signals.reasoning: The centering defect is fixed by leaving the funding ratio in its natural units, so the signal crosses zero exactly at zero net external financing and net payers score negative as claimed, rather than at an industry median. The two remaining changes from the archived competitive-slide signal are economic rather than cosmetic: financing is normalized by the research budget it funds instead of by assets, and the competitive slide is measured over two years, which captures sustained displacement rather than one noisy year of rank change.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ), rank( neg( sub( ind_rank( ratio( xrd, sale ) ), lag( ind_rank( ratio( xrd, sale ) ), 2 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
input_signals.hypothesis: Within research-active firms, the mix between acquired and self-generated innovation is informative: a firm adding far more goodwill than it spends on its own research is purchasing other people's ideas at negotiated premia, and equity raised to support that strategy is the most overvaluation-prone financing of all.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen-2's goodwill test failed in portfolios because the COALESCE weight created a huge tied mass across the whole market; here goodwill additions are normalized by the firm's own research budget inside the R&D-reporter universe that every surviving signal lives in, which makes the weight continuous and the comparison a genuine build-versus-buy composition rather than a goodwill-intensity level. It is the only conditioner in the archive that measures the *source* of innovation rather than its level, trend, or competitive rank.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( winsor( ratio( delta( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), 1 ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Firms With an Erratic Research Commitment
input_signals.hypothesis: A stable research budget reflects a managed portfolio of projects with credible internal funding, whereas a research budget that lurches up and down reveals opportunistic, funding-driven spending; equity raised by such firms is financing an unstable program that is likely to be abandoned.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen-1 tested the second moment of the *financing* series and found nothing (t -0.98), but the second moment of the *research* series is a different economic object — project-portfolio instability rather than funding lumpiness — and it has never been tried in this archive. It uses the validated architecture with a continuous, tie-free weight, and it discriminates a distinct pathology from Signals 1-2: erratic commitment versus measured decline.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( vol( ratio( xrd, sale ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance While Research Has Retreated From Its Own Peak
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose absolute research spending sits far below its own five-year peak has retreated from innovation; equity raised in that state cannot plausibly be funding the research program, so the proceeds are either plugging a hole or being sold on a story the firm has already stopped investing in.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the mechanical rank-average with a distinct economic state — absolute retreat from the firm's own research high-water mark — which is not what either parent conditioner measures: revenue-per-research-dollar can improve during a retreat, and industry rank slides can occur while spending still rises. The distance-from-own-extreme construction is new to this archive, is continuous and tie-free, and needs only five years of R&D history, so coverage stays at the level of the surviving family rather than falling further.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( ratio( xrd, ts_max( xrd, 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance After Research Failed to Convert Into Sales
input_signals.hypothesis: The test of a research program is whether the money spent two years ago shows up as revenue today; a firm whose sales growth falls well short of the research expansion it undertook two years earlier has a demonstrated conversion failure, and equity raised on the back of that program is being sold on an unfulfilled promise.
input_signals.reasoning: Comparing current sales growth directly against the firm's own lagged research growth makes the conditioner a conversion-shortfall measure rather than a sales trend with R&D in the denominator, which is the substantive objection to the gen-2 conditioner. It also requires only about four years of R&D history instead of the eight implied by trending a lagged moving average, so coverage should hold near the family's 5% rather than thinning further.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), lag( growth( xrd, 1 ), 2 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Firms Whose Research Outruns Internal Funds
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically relevant intangible state is whether the research budget can be paid for out of the firm's own gross margin; when research dwarfs internally generated funds the program survives only at the market's discretion, and equity raised in that position is financing a burn rather than an investment decision.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the knowledge-stock conditioner that the critic correctly identified as a sign-reversed R&D-intensity anomaly conflicting with the archive's ratio evidence, and replaces it with internal funding capacity — gross profit per research dollar — a variable never used in this archive and one that is consistent with, rather than contradictory to, the finding that financing is most damaging where the research program is not self-supporting. The weight is a bounded rank of a winsorized coverage ratio with an always-positive denominator among R&D reporters, so it introduces no new tied masses or scale blowups.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Proceeds Grew the Balance Sheet, Not the Research
input_signals.hypothesis: When a research firm raises equity, the informative fact is where the money went: if total assets expand far faster than the research budget, the proceeds financed acquisitions, cash hoards or working capital rather than the innovation program the equity story was sold on.
input_signals.reasoning: Every conditioner tried so far measures the *quality* of the research franchise; this measures the *destination of the proceeds*, which is the one dimension of the task's economic question — productive innovation funding versus opportunistic issuance — that the archive has never directly observed. It is also the natural response to gen-5's gate result: if franchise quality carries no independent cross-sectional information, use-of-proceeds may, because it is measured contemporaneously with the raise rather than as a slow-moving firm characteristic.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( winsor( sub( growth( at, 1 ), growth( xrd, 1 ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Firms With a Short Research Track Record
input_signals.hypothesis: Credibility comes from persistence: a firm that has reported research spending in only one or two of the last five years has no verifiable innovation history, so equity sold on an innovation narrative there is the least monitorable and most likely to be story-driven.
input_signals.reasoning: Track-record length is a credibility dimension distinct from every level, trend, competitive-rank and volatility conditioner already tested, and it is available for firms with sparse research histories that the trend-based conditioners mechanically exclude, so it should add coverage rather than subtract it. It also provides a clean check on whether the family's results are driven by long-established research firms or by intermittent reporters, which matters for interpreting the whole archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( ts_count( xrd, 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance Amid Commoditization and Research Retreat
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(WINSOR(SUB(TREND(RATIO(cogs, sale), 3), TREND(RATIO(xrd, sale), 3)), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose cost of goods is claiming a rising share of revenue while its research is claiming a falling share is being commoditized and is disinvesting from the very differentiation that could reverse it; equity raised in that configuration funds a business losing its intangible edge on both the cost and the innovation margin.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioner joins the cost side of the income statement, never used in this archive's surviving family, to the research side in a single differenced trend, so it is not the industry-normalization variant the critic rejected and it preserves the financing leg's economically meaningful zero point at zero net issuance. Requiring xrd keeps the signal inside the R&D-reporter universe where the mechanism has demonstrated portfolio alpha, avoiding the gen-4 broad-universe failure where a margin-based conditioner produced a strong FMB slope but no alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( winsor( sub( trend( ratio( cogs, sale ), 3 ), trend( ratio( xrd, sale ), 3 ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance by Firms Whose Intangible Base Was Purchased
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), TS_SUM(xrd, 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The share of a firm's intangible base that was bought rather than built is a standing measure of its innovation strategy; firms whose knowledge assets are mostly purchased goodwill have repeatedly paid acquisition premia instead of generating ideas, and equity raised to continue that strategy should be the most overvaluation-prone.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's best single signal is the build-versus-buy *flow* (alpha -2.5%, t -2.72, Sharpe -0.50), whose acknowledged weakness is a large tied mass at zero for firms with no goodwill activity in a given year; expressing composition as a stock share in [0,1] gives every firm a distinct position, eliminates the event-timing noise, and should stabilize portfolio membership. It also converts an event conditioner into a persistent strategy characteristic, which lowers turnover and tests whether the effect is about deal timing or about a durable acquisitive innovation model.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), ts_sum( xrd, 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Shareholder Cash In Minus Research Dollars Added
input_signals.hypothesis: The single number that separates the task's two poles is the net dollar flow between shareholders and the research program: money taken in from shareholders beyond what was added to research is opportunistic financing, while research expansion funded without taking shareholder money is productive intangible investment.
input_signals.reasoning: This is one continuous measure with an economically meaningful zero, not a rank-sum of two archived signals, and it differs from the gen-0 surplus construction by comparing financing against the *increment* to research rather than its level, which is the correct marginal comparison and removes the mechanical tilt toward research-intensive firms that the level version carried. Both tails are economically named — issuers who did not expand research at one end, self-funded research expanders at the other — so no leg is a residual pool.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), ratio( delta( xrd, 1 ), at ) ), 2 )

input_signals.name: Research Financed by Non-Debt Liabilities
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms can fund a research program without touching capital markets by stretching payables and other non-debt obligations; a large increase in non-debt liabilities relative to the research budget means the innovation program is being carried by counterparties, which is a fragile funding source that reverses when suppliers tighten.
input_signals.reasoning: Total liabilities net of interest-bearing debt is a financing channel this archive has never used, and expressing its change per research dollar keeps the measure genuinely cross-theme while leaving the well-worn issuance and repurchase variables out of the expression entirely. It sits in the ratio family that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes, with an always-positive denominator among R&D reporters and industry ranking to absorb sector differences in working-capital norms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( lt, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 1 ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Three-Year Raise With No Research Deployment
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(sstk, prstkc), 3), at), 2), RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(xrd, at), LAG(RATIO(xrd, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that has raised equity repeatedly over three years while its research intensity is no higher than it was three years ago never deployed the money into the innovation program it was raising against; the promised investment simply did not happen.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioner is not a contemporaneous state variable like every accepted conditioner in the archive but a matched-horizon audit — the change in research intensity measured over exactly the window in which the money was raised — which makes the interaction a deployment failure rather than a franchise-quality amplifier, and it is not entangled with the financing leg the way the book-equity conditioner was. Paired with Signal 2 it brackets the deployment mechanism from both poles, so the two together identify whether verified use of proceeds is what the market misprices.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( sub( sstk, prstkc ), 3 ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( sub( ratio( xrd, at ), lag( ratio( xrd, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance Amid Purchased-Intangible Churn
input_signals.hypothesis: Large movement in purchased intangibles in either direction — big acquisitions or big write-offs — relative to the firm's own research budget marks a deal-driven rather than organic innovation strategy; equity raised by such firms funds a serial dealmaking process whose track record already includes reversals.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive tested goodwill *additions* (alpha -2.5%) but never the magnitude of goodwill movement, and using ABS turns a directional flow into an activity measure so that impairment years — the revelation of failed prior deals — enter the short leg alongside acquisition years instead of being pushed to the long leg where they economically do not belong. Scaling by the firm's own research budget keeps the comparison a strategy-composition measure inside the R&D-reporter universe where portfolio alpha has consistently survived.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( winsor( ratio( abs( delta( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), 1 ) ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Share of the Research Budget Covered by Outside Money
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically bounded question is what fraction of this year's research program could have been paid for out of money raised from outside investors; a program essentially fully covered by external funds is a program that continues only while capital markets stay open, whereas one covered marginally is substantially self-financed.
input_signals.reasoning: Capping the external inflow at the size of the research budget converts the archive's unbounded funding-per-research multiple — whose extreme deciles are dominated by a handful of enormous raises — into a coverage share in roughly the unit interval, which is exactly the outlier problem behind that signal's strong FMB slope but modest alpha. Using gross inflows rather than net flows also means the measure does not cancel against repayments, so it is a different object from the archived net-external-finance ratio rather than a dividend-for-debt substitution into an existing template.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( min( add( dltis, sstk ), xrd ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance as Total Soft-Capital Spending Retreats
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), TS_MAX(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible investment is not only research: for consumer and services firms the brand budget plays the identical role, so the informative state is retreat from the firm's own peak in total soft-capital spending, research plus advertising, and equity raised during such a retreat funds a franchise the firm has itself stopped supporting.
input_signals.reasoning: Advertising is the one intangible variable in the resource menu this archive has never used, and treating an unreported line as zero spending is the economically correct convention when the other line is reported, so the conditioner extends the retreat mechanism to brand-driven firms and should widen the R&D-reporter universe that has constrained every result to about 5% coverage. It is a change in the definition of intangible capital rather than a re-scaling of an existing measure, and it directly tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about soft capital generally.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), ts_max( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Returned With Research and Margin Both Building
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MIN(RATIO(DELTA(xrd, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), at))), 2)
input_signals.hypothesis: The fully productive state requires three things at once: cash genuinely returned to shareholders on a net basis, a research budget being expanded, and gross profit rising to validate that the intangible investment is working; a firm satisfying all three is self-financing an innovation program whose output is already visible.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than lengthening the horizon of the archived long-pole signal — a parameter change that would mostly load on size and growth persistence — this adds an independent output-verification leg, gross profit growth, so that research expansions unaccompanied by any realized margin improvement no longer qualify. The nested MIN keeps all three arguments as identically asset-scaled dollar flows, and netting issuance out of the repurchase leg removes firms whose buybacks merely offset option-related issuance, which was the main contamination in the one-year version.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( min( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ), min( ratio( delta( xrd, 1 ), at ), ratio( delta( sub( sale, cogs ), 1 ), at ) ) ), 2 )

input_signals.name: Net Cash Returned With Research Expanding
input_signals.hypothesis: The productive pole is a firm that is a genuine net returner of cash — not one whose buybacks merely offset option issuance — while simultaneously adding dollars to its research budget, since only that combination demonstrates surplus cash generation alongside continued innovation investment.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive brackets this precisely: the gross-buyback version delivered the alpha (+2.2%, t +2.06) but a weak slope, while the triple conjunction with a margin leg delivered a strong slope (+2.85) but no alpha, indicating that netting issuance out of the payout leg is the useful part and the third leg over-restricts the sample. This two-leg net version is the untested interpolation between two evaluated points and is the archive's best remaining chance at a long pole with joint support.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( min( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ), ratio( delta( xrd, 1 ), at ) ), 2 )

input_signals.name: Issuance While Purchased Technology Amortizes Away
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(intan, 1), DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Separating the intangible balance into goodwill and identifiable intangibles reveals whether purchased technology, patents and customer relationships are being replenished or simply amortized away; a firm whose identifiable intangibles are eroding relative to its research budget is losing acquired capability, and equity raised in that state funds a shrinking asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic blend of two goodwill measures with a decomposition of the intangible balance sheet that the archive has never used — the change in intangibles net of the change in goodwill isolates identifiable intangible assets, whose amortization is economically distinct from goodwill activity and from research spending. The conditioner is continuous, research-scaled and free of the tied mass that the goodwill-flow weights carry for firms with no deal activity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 2 ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( intan, 1 ), delta( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), 1 ) ), ma( xrd, 3 ) ), 5 ) ) ) )
